project.name: Courier
project.description: Book a parcel pickup, pay for it, and track it to the door.

setup.services/api/app/main.py:
import logging

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

from app.logging_setup import configure
from app.routes import assistant, health, parcels, payments

configure()
log = logging.getLogger("courier.requests")

app = FastAPI(title="Courier API")


@app.middleware("http")
async def log_requests(request: Request, call_next):
    response = await call_next(request)
    log.info(f"{request.method} {request.url.path} returned {response.status_code}")
    return response


app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["*"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

app.include_router(parcels.router)
app.include_router(payments.router)
app.include_router(assistant.router)
app.include_router(health.router)
setup.ops/alerts.yml:
# Alerts, sent to the team's chat channel.
alerts:
  - name: any-server-error
    when: count(status >= 500) > 0 over 1m
    notify: "#courier-alerts"
  - name: busy-cpu
    when: cpu > 50% over 1m
    notify: "#courier-alerts"

prompts.observability-review: Review how Courier is watched in production.

defects.title: Request logs are sentences built by pasting values together, not fields a search can filter on
Requests carry no id, so a customer's failed booking can't be followed through the logs
The health check says ok whatever happens, so the load balancer keeps sending traffic when the database is down
Alerts fire on a single server error and on a busy CPU, and say nothing about what to do, so people learn to ignore them
There are no written targets for booking, paying or tracking, so nothing warns before they fail people
